label: Tighten
instruction: Tighten slide {{SLIDE}}: at most five bullets, at most ten words each, and cut every word that is not carrying a fact. Keep the meaning and keep the numbers.

label: Make it a claim
instruction: Rewrite the title of slide {{SLIDE}} so it states the point instead of naming the topic — "Churn is a pricing problem", not "Churn analysis". Leave the bullets alone unless the new title makes one redundant.
help: Title states the point, not the topic

label: Speaker notes
instruction: Write the speaker notes for slide {{SLIDE}}. Say what the presenter SAYS, not what the slide shows: expand the bullets into spoken sentences, add the detail behind each claim, and end with the transition into the next slide. Never restate the bullets. Do not change the slide itself.
help: What you say, not what the slide shows

label: Make it visual
instruction: Slide {{SLIDE}} is text where it could be a picture. Pick the ONE form that fits what the bullets say: if one number carries the point, a bigFact slide with that number and a one-line label; if it compares two things, twoColumn with the compared items as the first entry of each column; if the user's Ledger has a collection that evidences it, a chart bound to that collection; if it names parts that connect, a process with an order, a cycle, levels, stages that narrow, overlapping groups or a two-by-two, a diagram slide (the diagram grammar: flow, rows, hub, loop, pyramid, funnel, cycle, venn, matrix or ladder), using the slide's own words as the labels and nothing the slide does not say; if it is ordered actions, steps; if it is dated events, timeline. Otherwise leave the layout alone and say why in your reply.
help: Re-flow into a big number, comparison, chart or diagram

label: Make it a diagram
instruction: Turn slide {{SLIDE}} into a diagram slide (layout diagram) that shows what its bullets describe. Choose the diagram kind from the content: flow for a process or a request path, rows for layers, hub for one thing and its parts, cycle for a repeating loop of stages, pyramid for levels that build on each other, funnel for stages that narrow, venn for two or three overlapping groups, matrix for a two-by-two with named axes, ladder for steps that rise. Every label comes from the slide's own title, bullets or notes, shortened, never invented; keep the title; move any bullet the diagram cannot hold into the speaker notes. Twelve boxes or fewer. If the slide has nothing a diagram can show, leave it alone and say why in your reply.
help: Boxes, arrows, cycles, pyramids — from this slide's own words

label: Add evidence
instruction: Slide {{SLIDE}} asserts something without support. Add the number, date or source that backs it — but ONLY from the deck's own material or the user's Ledger collections listed in your context. If nothing supports it, say so in your reply and change nothing: an invented statistic is worse than a thin slide.
help: Back the claim — never invent one

label: Split
instruction: Slide {{SLIDE}} is carrying more than one idea. Split it into two slides in place, each with one claim as its title, and divide the existing bullets between them. Add nothing new.
